## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01 and REQ-02 fail: the projected lock scope is inaccurate, and the shipped coordination template retains unchecked default copies. REQ-03 is covered by the committed-reference conformance test.

## Architecture and functional style

No layer-boundary or functional-style regression found.

## Correctness and safety

No unsafe-code, PID-safety, event-log, or atomic-write regression found.

## Testing

Recorded `cargo-ci` and `docs-mechanical` gates passed. I did not rerun Cargo tests as instructed. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed.

## Error handling and CLI contract

No regression found; JSON support remains intact.

## Documentation

The reference is generated and discoverable, but its lock scope overstates coverage. The generated project configuration also retains coordination-default facts outside the projection.

## JIT issue management

The sole dependency is done. The latest prior-review heartbeat finding is addressed; the lock-scope finding remains unresolved in a different form.

## Findings

1. **High** — [runtime_defaults.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/runtime_defaults.rs:131) says `JsonFileStorage` holds its environment-configured storage locks “for all `.jit` data writes.” This is false: [save_gate_run_result](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:780) and [save_gate_preset](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:940) write under no `FileLocker` or repository write lock. The generated projection therefore still gives an inaccurate operational scope for `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, failing REQ-01.

2. **Medium** — [hierarchy_templates.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/hierarchy_templates.rs:267) ships user-facing coordination-template comments with independent `600`-second claim TTL and `30`-second heartbeat defaults. They neither consume `runtime_defaults` nor have a conformance check, so either can drift when the projected defaults change, failing REQ-02.

Total findings: 2
